summary: T. N. Ramachandran (1901–1973) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an archaeologist at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1925–1934) and as curator of archaeology at the National Museum, New Delhi, teaching Ramaa Bharadvaj and Padma Subrahmanyam.

Indologist T. R. Chintamani earned his Ph.D. at the University of Madras under S. Kuppuswami Sastri. He served as Librarian of the Eastern Section at Adyar Library (~1927–1930) and Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1933).

T. R. V. Murti (1902–1986) worked in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, earning a D.Litt. at Banaras Hindu University under Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He held posts at Oxford (~1949–1950), BHU (~1953–1967), and McMaster University (~1968–1972).
T. S. Devadoss is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He held posts at the University of Madras, where his affiliation is attested in 1994 and his role as Professor is attested in 2008.

T. S. Eliot (1888–1965) studied philosophy and other subjects at Milton Academy, Harvard, Paris, and Merton College, under teachers including George Santayana and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He later held posts at Birkbeck (~1917–1919) and the University of Chicago (~1950).

T. S. Rukmani (b. 1932) is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. She held posts at Miranda House (attested 1983–1989) and Concordia University, where she chaired Hindu Studies in the Department of Religion (attested 1989).

Indologist and philosopher T. S. Srinivasa Sastri taught Robert P. Goldman, N. Veezhinathan, Yoshitsugu Sawai, and Ludo Rocher. He held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1972, as Professor 1984–1992, and 2007).

T. Shrinivas Shastri is an Indology scholar who taught Robert P. Goldman and Sally J. Sutherland Goldman. He held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, attested as Pandit in 1993 and as Professor in 2026.

T. V. Ramachandra Dikshitar worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Principal at Madras Sanskrit College (attested 1938) and as Professor of Advaita Vedanta at Banaras Hindu University (attested 1946).

T. V. Vasudeva is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who taught S. N. Krishna. He held positions at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute as an Editorial Committee member (attested 2001) and Deputy Director (attested 2026).

T. V. Venkatachala Sastry (b. 1933) studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Mysore under D. L. Narasimhachar and H. M. Nayak, among others. He taught at several institutions before serving as Professor at Mysore (1984–1994).

Indologist T. Venkatacharya held posts at the Italian Institute for Africa and the East (attested 1971) and as Professor at the University of Toronto (attested 1971–1979). He taught Yuichi Kajiyama, Shoryu Katsura, Richard P. Hayes, and Amar Singh.

T. W. Rhys Davids (1843–1922) earned his Ph.D. at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, he founded the Pali Text Society and held professorships at University of London and Owens College/Manchester.
T. Y. Lee is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed studies at Mangala Vihara Buddhist Temple and the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Tadao Yoshikawa (b. 1937) studied at Kyoto University, working in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He served as assistant professor at Kyoto University (1974, 1984–2000), professor at Ryukoku University (2002), and president of Toho Gakkai (~2005–2011).

Tadashi Inoue (1929–2014) studied at the University of Tokyo, specializing in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyoto National Museum (1967, 1979), Nara University (1987), Iida City Museum (1988–2006), Bukkyo University (1995), and Kyoto University of the Arts (2000).

Tadashi Sekino (1868–1935) was a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1892–1895) and later served there as Professor Emeritus (~1929–1935).

Tadashi Tani (b. 1941) studied at Waseda University and Kyoto University under Yuichi Kajiyama in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He was a professor at Kochi College (attested 1996–2000) and later lectured part-time at several universities in 2012.
Tadashi Toda is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Keiki Higashimoto and Kogen Mizuno.

Linguist Tadeusz Milewski (1906–1966) earned his Ph.D. at Lviv, completed habilitation at Jagiellonian University, and studied under Rozwadowski, Willman-Grabowska, Meillet, Vendryes, and Benveniste. He was a professor of general linguistics at KUL (1945–1950) and Jagiellonian University (1949–1966).
